text: Select the Data Flow Debug toggle right on the canvas top bar, and you're prompted to choose an integration runtime configuration. Picking AutoResolveIntegrationRuntime spins up a genuinely small cluster by default, with a sixty-minute time to live before it shuts itself down.

Raise that time to live if you want more idle time before the session actually times out — genuinely useful during a long design session where you're stepping away between edits. The cluster status indicator turns green the moment it's ready — nearly instant if it was already warm, a few minutes if it needed a cold boot.

With debug turned on, the Data Preview tab lights up on every single transformation — a real, interactive snapshot of the actual data sitting at that exact point in the stream. Select Refresh to update it based on your current transformations, or Refresh, Refetch from source if the underlying data itself actually changed.

This is genuinely worth remembering: debug mode never writes to a sink at all. It's a test harness for your transformation logic, sampled entirely in Spark memory — nothing lands anywhere real until you actually run the data flow from a pipeline instead.

Every debug session spins up its own separate Spark cluster, billed hourly for the entire time it's running, including that idle time-to-live period. Turn the toggle off the moment you're genuinely done working — leaving it on just in case quietly keeps billing in the background. Next: Source and Sink transformations — the two real ends of every data flow, configured properly.
